questions.question: Absolute figures like R7 900 carry no verdict because:
options: A figure only gains meaning against a BASE — spectacular for a spaza table, catastrophic for a supermarket
Only percentages are legal in statements
Rand amounts change with inflation daily

questions.question: Every profitability percentage asks:
options: How fast is the stock selling?
Out of every hundred rand of SALES, how many rand ended up as this?
How much cash is in the bank?

questions.question: The formula sheet means the examined skills are:
options: SELECTION of the right formula, correct SUBSTITUTION, and INTERPRETATION

questions.question: The commonest calculation error in this topic is:
options: Feeding the WRONG FIGURE into a right formula — operating profit where net belongs, cost of sales where sales belongs

questions.question: Gross profit on SALES for the year is:
options: 20 000 / 100 000 × 100 = 20% — twenty rand of margin from every hundred over the counter

questions.question: Gross profit on COST OF SALES computes to 25%, which is recognisable as:
options: THE MARK-UP — the pricing policy of 25% on cost, confirmed by actual trading
The interest rate on the loan

questions.question: The two gross percentages are:
options: The SAME profit read from the two ends of the counter — mark-up applied on cost, margin received on sales
Only different when there are errors

questions.question: Achieved mark-up 21% against policy 25% signals:
options: The policy must be reduced to 21%
A FINDING — markdowns, stock lost after costing, recording errors or theft; the gap sizes the leak

subtopics.title: The Operating Family and Net Profit on Sales

questions.question: Operating expenses on sales is:
A RISING expense percentage across years means:
options: Sales are growing faster than expenses
Expenses are growing FASTER than sales — the operating leak; the itemised list says which line swells

questions.question: The distance between operating profit (9,1%) and net profit (7,9%) isolates:
options: The FINANCING bite — the loan's interest as a share of every hundred rand of sales

questions.question: The dashboard read as one glance:
options: Mark-up 25 achieved; margin 20; expenses 17; operations keep 9; owner keeps 8 — the earning story in portable proportions

questions.question: The three comparison bases are:
options: LAST YEAR (trend), the POLICY (control check), a SIMILAR BUSINESS (competitive check)
The bank, the auditor and SARS

questions.question: The comment's four-move anatomy is:
options: STATE the figure and comparison; JUDGE favourable/unfavourable; EXPLAIN the likely cause from the scenario; RECOMMEND one action

questions.question: "It went down" as a full answer earns:
options: Only the first quarter of the marks — the STATE move without judge, explain or recommend

questions.question: Respecting what each percentage CAN say means:
options: Using every percentage in every answer
Gross percentages speak of pricing and stock control, the expense percentage of cost management — diagnose from the right gauge

questions.question: Following one hundred-rand note through the year gives:
options: R80 replaces the goods, R20 margin, nearly R17 runs the shop, R7,90 remains as the owner's keep
R50 to stock, R50 to the owner
R20 to tax, R80 to wages

questions.question: Percentages "travel" and rand totals don't because:
options: Per-hundred proportions can be compared with any year and any business; totals are trapped in their own year

questions.question: The five official percentages are:
options: The checkpoint names along the hundred-rand note's journey

subtopics.title: The Health Check at the Clinic

questions.question: "Temperature 37 — fine or fever?" teaches that:
options: A vital sign means nothing until COMPARED — against the normal range or your own last visit
All percentages have one healthy value

questions.question: Margin fine but the owner's keep thin points to:
options: The RUNNING COSTS — some expense line is swelling; the problem is not pricing

questions.question: Margin down but expenses steady points to:
options: An UPSTREAM leak — markdowns, missing stock, prices slipping

questions.question: The percentages "never treat anything" but:
options: They tell you WHICH ORGAN to examine, and catch sickness while it's curable

questions.question: The four-line recipe in home language is:
options: WHAT happened; SO what (verdict); WHY (from the story); NOW WHAT (action)

questions.question: Line three's WHY must come from:
options: THE SCENARIO — supplied clues like markdowns or a break-in; analysis is detective work with given evidence

questions.question: Asked about pricing, the right gauges are:
options: The GROSS percentages — margin on sales and mark-up on cost

questions.question: The interpretation error markers see most is:
options: Answering from the WRONG GAUGE — the percentage that cannot speak to the question asked
